tracker.company: Maine Department of Administrative & Financial Services (OIT)
tracker.research_notes: Seeded 2026-09-30 from Claude's general knowledge; not verified.

triage.why: Maine state IT; senior QA/test roles likely, public-sector stability; remote/hybrid possible in Maine.
triage.flags: State pay; remote may be hybrid only

remote_policy.summary: The department publishes teleworking/remote access security guidance: use a state-provided computer, connect it to home Wi-Fi, and follow state I.T. rules wherever you work.

signals.summary: Maine's FY 2026 biennial state budget, which funds state agencies including DAFS/OIT, was enacted for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2025.

fit.rationale: Maine's central IT agency runs and tests statewide systems (health, benefits, tax), so senior QA roles are plausible but rare and mostly in Augusta, ~1.5 hours from Bangor. Public-sector durability is excellent; the candidate's Maine residency and regulated V&V background

research.approach_role: State CIO / Director, Office of Information Technology
research.outreach_angle: Your FDA-regulated V&V and design-controls experience maps directly to testing Maine's health, benefits and eligibility systems, and you live in-state, so hybrid or telework arrangements are workable.
research.red_flags: No QA openings listed; state hiring is slow and openings skew toward Augusta, not Downeast Maine.
research.notes: Verified: DAFS/OIT publishes telework security guidance (state laptop, home Wi-Fi, state IT rules) but does not state Maine-residency eligibility. FY2026 biennial budget funds the agency, a strong stability signal. No QA openings or named QA leaders were found, so openings must be checked directly.
